deviation_from_the_lock: The DEV-1000 BLEND lock embedded the trajectory's OWN direct answer IN FLIGHT (launch_dev1000_baseline_lock.py's RuntimeEmbeddedBlendController). This pass embeds a SEALED prior run's answer to the same question for the same row, before takeoff. Same embedder, same signal family, different provenance: a pre-flight vector cannot see a flight's own phase-1 answer. The lock's own recall signal was text-only too, which is exactly what the 2026-09-06 owner rule now forbids as a retrieval query -- so this receipt records a property of the LOCK as much as of this pass.
embedded_signal: TEXT-ONLY, and therefore NOT a legal retrieval query under the owner rule of 2026-09-06: the SEALED phase-1 ('draft') response text of each DEV-1000 row of run SAEA-SLURP-KU-S1C-DRAFT-REVISE-DEV1000-V1 (attempt attempt-20260906T042946Z-44720f, phases file sha256 f6ed3c14...264e63), embedded once before the flight by the pinned tool-level embedder qwen3-embedding-0.6b-gguf (Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B-Q8_0.gguf, sha256 06507c7b...e439, 1,024 dimensions, llama.cpp featcache 04ccc72a, --embedding --pooling last, -ngl 0, CPU only). This reproduces the SIGNAL the DEV-1000 BLEND lock recalled on -- a direct-decode answer's embedding -- from a SEALED prior run instead of in flight. KU-S1c's draft phase is the closest sealed stand-in for KU-S1's own phase 1: same phase-program path, same byte-identical closed-list system message, same static directive probes/slurp_phase_direct.txt. The one deviation, stated and not hidden: the pre-flight vector cannot see THIS flight's own phase-1 answer.

source.fields_not_read: everything else: no gold, no reference transcript, no SLURP devel sentence text, no audio, no other run's material

storage.note: vectors are written EXACTLY as the pinned llama.cpp server returned them (that server L2-normalizes pooled embeddings by default, which the measured norms confirm). Each float32 is widened to the exactly equal Python float and serialised with the shortest decimal that round-trips that double.
